status_definitions.partial: Partially evidenced by approved repository evidence.
status_definitions.not_applicable: Not applicable based on approved scope evidence.

evidence_policy.confidence_notes: Green and yellow source annotations are preserved as source_note values. They are confidence notes, not evidence.
evidence_policy.evidence_bindings: Evidence-backed answers require approved manifest bindings whose attestations cover the exact control ID, status, statement, and complete binding-ID set.
evidence_policy.regulations: The source stated that regulations were collapsed but did not supply their values; null preserves that omission.

controls.name: Business Impact Analysis
controls.description: A criticality assessment (CA) is completed to identify mission critical processes. Subsequently, a business impact analysis (BIA) is documented for mission critical processes to determine resource requirements for resiliency. The CA and BIA are reviewed and approved.

answer.missing_evidence: Approved fortlogs criticality assessment and process-level business impact analysis, including review records.

controls.name: Process Continuity
controls.description: In accordance with the Business Continuity Management Security Standard, a Process Continuity Plan (PCP) is documented and maintained for each mission critical business process – providing procedures for sustaining operations while recovering from a significant disruption. The plan is reviewed, approved and communicated to all named stakeholders.

answer.missing_evidence: Approved fortlogs Process Continuity Plan, maintenance history, and stakeholder communication records.

controls.name: Approve user Access Request
controls.description: All access to systems in scope is requested via the access management tool. Each access request is assessed by the authorized approvers. The approver defines the validity of the access up to the profile dependent maximum validity. The access can be declined by: approvers revoking manually, validity expiring, or account invalidation (user left SAP).

answer.source_note: 🟢 yes should be done through the permission system and CAM2? I guess we need to find proof of how fortlogs conforms to these CAM profiles.
answer.missing_evidence: Fortlogs CAM2 profiles, request workflow, approver mapping, maximum-validity settings, and revocation or expiry samples.

controls.name: Review of Administrators
controls.description: Only a limited number of authorized persons have access rights to administer the access management tool (including assigning users to approver roles). Bi-annually the Management reviews the list of administrators and all approvers maintained in the access management tool. The authorized users are extended and unauthorized users are removed.

answer.source_note: 🟡 not sure how CAM2 does it here.
answer.missing_evidence: CAM2 administrator and approver lists, restricted-admin configuration, semi-annual management review, and removal records.

controls.name: Password configuration
controls.description: SAP users are required to log on to the SAP clients using their user SAP Domain credentials (user ID and password) before access is granted. The authentication configuration is set according to the SAP Password Policy requirements (length, complexity, validity, history, multi-factor etc.).

answer.source_note: 🟡 I guess that is true, you need proper SAP creds to get in (authentication). and once you get in your CAM2 profile and thus access to fortlogs is granted (authorization).
answer.missing_evidence: Fortlogs authentication flow, SAP Domain integration, effective password-policy settings, multi-factor enforcement, and CAM2 authorization mapping.
